# Sources this skill cites

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-adjustment-items

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.b: adjusted DSC items, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Adjustments to cash flow the lender may justify include unfunded capex, non-recurring income, distributions, S-corp tax distributions, seller discretionary expenses and owner compensation.
- **Quote:** "Justification for additions and subtractions to cash flow, such as the following: Unfunded capital expenditures; Non-recurring income; Distributions; Distributions for S-Corp taxes; Seller discretionary expenses; and/or Ownership Compensation."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-adjustment-justification

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.b: justifying adjustments, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The lender must justify each adjustment as prudent, necessary and supported by ongoing operations.
- **Quote:** "When using adjustments, the Lender must outline why each adjustment is prudent, necessary, and how it can be supported by the ongoing operations of the business."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-adjustments

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: cash-flow adjustments, U.S. Small Business Administration

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-dsc-definition

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: definition of historical DSC, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Historical debt service coverage is EBITDA divided by all debt service after the transaction, not only the SBA loan payment.
- **Quote:** "The historical DSC ratio is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) divided by the combined debt service post-transaction."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-dsc-ratio

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15 (7(a) Changes of Ownership), Para. C.2: debt service coverage, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For a 7(a) change of ownership, the lender tests debt service coverage on the last fiscal year-end or the average of the last two, at 1.25:1 for an initial acquisition or owner buyout and 1.15:1 for a business expansion.
- **Quote:** "The Debt Service Coverage (DSC) ratio must be satisfied using either the last fiscal year-end or an average of the last two fiscal year-end statements on either a historical or adjusted basis based on the transaction type: Initial Acquisition: 1.25:1 Business Expansion: 1.15:1 Owner Buyout: 1.25:1 ESOP and Cooperative: 1.25:1"
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-equity-project-cost

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: equity based on total project cost, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** The equity injection is measured against total project cost, not just the purchase price.
- **Quote:** "SBA requires equity injections (Applicant contribution) for change of ownership transactions to be based on the total project cost (all costs required to become operational, regardless of the source of funds, except for lines of credit and 504 loans)."

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-interest-only-debt

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.b: interest-only debt in coverage, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For coverage, the lender treats interest-only acquisition debt (such as a seller note not on standby) as if it amortized over no more than 10 years.
- **Quote:** "When a change of ownership transaction includes additional debt to support the purchase that is not on full standby and is structured with interest-only payments, the Lender must apply an amortization that does not exceed 10-years."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-projections

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: projections, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In a 7(a) change of ownership the lender may not rely on projections to meet the coverage requirement, except for an owner-occupied special purpose property.
- **Quote:** "The Lender must evaluate the Applicant's post-closing financial projections but may not rely on them to meet the DSC requirement. This limitation does not apply to a transaction involving the acquisition of an owner-occupied Special Purpose Property, which may be underwritten on the basis of projections as provided under Special Purpose Properties above."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-dsc

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: QoE findings drive debt service coverage, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** When a QoE is required, the lender calculates debt coverage from its findings and must reduce the loan if coverage doesn't support the deal.
- **Quote:** "When a change of ownership transaction requires a Quality of Earnings (QoE) report as part of the necessary financial due diligence, the Lender must use the report’s findings to calculate the Debt Service Coverage. If that Debt Service Coverage does not support the business valuation and proposed debt structure, the loan amount must be reduced accordingly."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-qoe-threshold

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: Quality of Earnings required at $3 million, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** For 7(a) initial acquisitions and business expansions with a business purchase price of $3 million or more, the lender must obtain a quality of earnings report as well as the business valuation, measured before equity, seller debt or other financing.
- **Quote:** "For Business Expansion and Initial Acquisition transactions where the Purchase Price as defined in Paragraph A.1 is equal to or greater than $3 million, the Lender must also obtain a Quality of Earnings (QoE) in addition to the required Business Valuation. The $3 million threshold is determined before the application of buyer equity, seller debt, or other financing sources."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-debt-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller debt as equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Seller debt counts as equity for SBA purposes only if it is subordinated and on full standby, with no principal or interest payments for the life of the 7(a) loan.
- **Quote:** "Seller debt that is subordinated to the Lender and on full standby (no payments of principal or interest for the term of the 7(a) loan) may be considered as equity for SBA’s purposes."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-standby-terms

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2.a: standby debt agreements, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Standby debt may accrue interest to be paid after the 7(a) loan is repaid, and the standby creditor must subordinate its liens and take no action without the lender’s consent.
- **Quote:** "The standby debt may accrue interest and may be added to the standby debt and amortized after the 7(a) loan is paid in full. Standby Creditor must subordinate any lien rights in collateral securing the loan to Lender’s rights in the collateral and take no action against Borrower or any collateral securing the Standby Debt without Lender’s consent."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-total-debt-cap

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: total debt limited to the valuation, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** All debt in an SBA acquisition, including seller debt not on full standby, is capped at the business valuation and must be covered by cash flow.
- **Quote:** "The total debt eligible to support a change of ownership transaction (including seller debt that is not on full standby) is limited to the business valuation amount and must be supported by the Debt Service Coverage of the Applicant."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-valuation-gap-equity

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: price above valuation is covered by equity, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** If the price is higher than the independent business valuation, the difference must come from equity, not more debt.
- **Quote:** "The business valuation must support the Business Purchase Price as defined in Paragraph A.1 regardless of how the debt is structured. If the amount paid for the business exceeds the business valuation, the difference must be made up by equity."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
